3.29.3
Description of the XVI table factors
If the treatment table is installed on a digital accelerator with X-Ray Volume Imaging (XVI) system
R3.5 or later, and the treatment table has been re-calibrated, then the XVI table factors must be
put into the XVI computer. See the applicable XVI Corrective Maintenance Manual.
When you do work on the digital accelerator, it can be necessary to calibrate the movement of
the gantry or the treatment table. The software for the digital accelerator does not automatically
send this changed calibration data to the XVI software. This causes errors to occur when XVI
calculates the table correction values, because the calibration data does not agree.
Therefore, it is important that you use the XVI DCB utility in the XVI software to copy the
applicable changed calibration data to the XVI software.

applicable changed calibration data to the XVI software. Use the XVI DCB utility in the XVI
software to copy the changed calibration data. If you ignore this warning, you can cause clinical
mistreatment.

4.1.8
Using the manual crank handle
If there are no motorized movements, operate the manual crank handle to lift or lower the
treatment table.
1 
Lower the bellows cover.
2 
Attach the manual crank handle to the output shaft of the height motor.
001898
©2013 Elekta Limited
Figure 4.17
Manual crank handle on the height motor shaft.
3 
Release the height motor brake. Follow one of these two procedures.
a
Use the brake release tool.
b
Attach a length of string or wire to the brake release handle.
4 
Pull the string or wire away from the brake release handle and along the axis of the height
motor.
5 
Turn the manual crank handle clockwise to lift the treatment table, or counterclockwise to
lower the treatment table.
Note:
800 turns of the crank handle is approximately equal to 1000 mm of movement.
6 
When the treatment table is in position, disengage the manual crank handle from the shaft
of the height motor.
Note:
800 turns of the crank handle is approximately equal to 1000 mm of movement.
WARNING 4.4
Do not use motorized movement of the treatment table until after you remove the manual
crank handle. If you ignore this warning, you can cause serious injury.
7 
If you used a string or wire to release the brake, remove these from the brake release
handle.

Defective potentiometers

Defective cables

Drive belts move from their usual position and become non-linear.

If
Then
LED 6 is ON

check potentiometer.

Make sure that the drive belts are in the correct position.
3 
Make sure that the movement of the potentiometers is linear through
its full range of movement.
LED 6 is OFF No correction is necessary.

5.1
Repair and replacement of the floor pan
5.1.1
Removing the floor pan with motorized movement of the treatment
table
Prerequisites
Hoist
Lifting jig
Lifting straps.
If motorized movement of the treatment table is available, you can use the treatment table to
help you to remove the floor pan. If motorized movement of the treatment table is not available,
do the procedure to remove the floor pan without motorized movement.
Before you try this procedure, make sure that you can use this procedure with third-party table
tops.
1 
Rotate the column assembly to 0°.
2 
Move the lateral carriage assembly to 0 mm.
3 
Move treatment table in the longitudinal direction until the table top is above the rotating
floor pan.
4 
Attach the straps to the table top and hang the lifting jig on the straps. Make sure that the
position of the bolt on the lifting jig is more in the direction of the treatment table.
5 
On the user interface module, operate the HEIGHT thumbwheel until the lifting jig is above
the center of the floor pan.

5.20.2
Installing a potentiometer in the lateral movement system
Prerequisites
Digital voltmeter.
1 
Move the lateral drive plate to the center position, and align the holes in the lateral drive
plate with the holes in the lateral drive subassembly.
2 
Install two screws to lock the lateral drive plate in position.
3 
At PCB835, connect the cable to the applicable plug:
–
PL3 (lateral movement coarse potentiometer)
–
PL4 (lateral movement fine potentiometer)
–
PL5 (lateral movement check potentiometer).
4 
Adjust the new potentiometer until the voltage is equal to 5 V (±10 mV).
5 
Put the potentiometer in position and install the nut and washer to attach the
potentiometer to the bracket.
Note:
Do not fully tighten the nut.
6 
Apply a small quantity of Loctite® 243™ to the threads of the set screw, and tighten the set
screw on the shaft of the potentiometer.
7 
Measure the voltage of the coarse or check potentiometer between pin 1 and 2.
8 
Rotate the drive gear of the new potentiometer to adjust the measured voltage until it is
equal to 5 V (±10 mV).
Note:
For a new fine potentiometer, you do not have to adjust the voltage.
9 
Tighten the 13mm nut and make sure that the voltage is equal to 5 V (±10 mV).
10 Remove the two screws that lock the lateral drive plate in position.
11 Install the longitudinal drive subassembly.
12 Remove the safety support struct.
13 Assemble the longitudinal carriage assembly.
14 Do the calibration of the longitudinal movement system.

5.26.1.2
Installing the height motor drive on the height drive gearbox
Prerequisites
Height drive motor toolkit.
This procedure is only applicable to treatment tables before Serial No. 126499, with an
Electrocraft motor.
1 
Remove unwanted grease from the coupling on the gearbox.
2 
Remove the flexible element from the coupling of the gearbox or the motor. Keep the
flexible element.
3 
Loosen the set screw that holds the coupling on the old height drive motor shaft.
4 
Remove the old coupling and flexible element from the motor shaft.
Note:
To remove the old coupling from the motor shaft can be difficult. If necessary, apply force to
remove it.
5 
Lubricate the new motor shaft with a thin layer of EP2 grease.
6 
Install the coupling on the new motor shaft.
7 
Move the coupling along the motor shaft until you can see the end of the motor shaft
through the coupling. Do not tighten the set screw at this time.
8 
Align the coupling on the motor shaft with the coupling in the gearbox shaft. Make sure that
the jaws of each coupling do not cause a collision.
9 
Put the motor into the gearbox and make sure that the front face of the motor touches with
the front face of the gearbox.
This will set the coupling on the motor shaft to the correct start position.
10 Remove the motor from the gearbox shaft, and then move the coupling on the motor shaft
1 mm in the direction of the motor.

5.31
Adjusting the height movement limit switches
5.31.1
Adjusting the upper limit switches of the height movement
mechanism
There are four limit switches and four adjustable actuators (two of each for the lower limit, and
the upper limit) installed on the height mechanism. The table top must be installed when you set
up the upper and lower limit switches.
1 
Set the column rotation to 0°.
2 
Lower the bellows cover.
3 
Attach a length of string or wire to the brake release handle of the height motor, this will let
you manually release the brake.
4 
On the user interface module, operate the HEIGHT thumbwheel to move the treatment
table up, until you can get access to the upper limit microswitches.
Note:
The upper limit microswitches are on the gun side of the upper arm assembly.
5 
Short circuit one of the two microswitches to disable its operation.
6 
Use the HEIGHT thumbwheel to lower the treatment table to the upper firmware limit
(minimum table height).
7 
Accurately measure the vertical distance between the upper surface of the table top and the
finished floor level. Record this distance as measurement H1.
Note:
The reference voltage for the minimum height H1 is defined in the Firmware of the LCU PCB in the
EIM cabinet. If the coarse and check potentiometers of the height mechanism are set incorrectly,
the treatment table can move to a very low position. If this occurs, the treatment table will
operate the limit switches.
8 
Pull the string or wire out along the axis of the height motor to manually release the brake.
9 
Turn the manual crank handle counterclockwise until the upper microswitch limit (minimum
table height) activates.
On the user interface module, the LEDs go off for three to five seconds.

10 Accurately measure the vertical distance between the upper surface of the table top and the
finished floor level. Record this distance as measurement H2.
11 Compare the measurements H1 and H2. If the coarse and check potentiometers are set
correctly, H1 will be 6 mm greater than H2.
12 Manually release the brake.
13 Turn the manual crank handle counterclockwise until the treatment table is at the upper
limit of mechanical travel.
14 At this point, you will feel an increased resistance as you turn the manual crank handle.
15 Accurately measure the vertical distance between the upper surface of the table top and the
finished floor level. Record this distance as measurement H3.
16 If the limit switches are set correctly, measurement H2 will be 2 mm to 3 mm greater than
H3 .
17 Manually release the brake.

18 Turn the manual crank handle clockwise to move the treatment table to a height that it is

19 Reset the STOP MOTORS inhibit, and move the table up as necessary.
20 Do steps 8 to 11 again, and use the activating screw on the gun side of the lower arm to
adjust the microswitch. Adjust the microswitch until the value of H2 is 2 mm to 3 mm
greater than H3.
21 Remove the short circuit from the microswitch. Then short circuit the other upper limit
microswitch to disable its operation.
22 Do steps 8 to 16 again for the other microswitch.
23 Make sure that the value of measurement H1 is a minimum of 6 mm greater than H2. If it is

Note:
If you adjust the coarse potentiometer, you must calibrate the height movement system.

5.33

5.33.1
Disconnecting the electrical interface module from the electrical
supply
There is no electrical power supply to the EIM cabinet when the digital accelerator is off. But if it
is on, there is an electrical power supply to the EIM cabinet.
WARNING 5.14
Do not do work on the EIM if it is connected to the electrical power supply. Always disconnect
the electrical supply before you start the work. If you ignore this warning, you can cause fatal
injury.
WARNING 5.15
Do not do work on the EIM cabinet with the covers removed, until you disconnect the electrical
supply. There are high voltages at the UPS, although the electrical supply to the EIM cabinet is
disconnected. If you ignore this warning, you can cause fatal injury.
All the steps of this procedure must be completed to remove the electrical supply to the EIM
cabinet.
1 
On the front panel of the EIM PSU, switch CB1 to OFF to disconnect the electrical supply to
the PSU.
The UPS continues to supply power to the PSU, and the amber lamp below CB1 stays on.
2 
On the front panel of the UPS, press the OFF button to disconnect the electrical supply to
the PSU.
On the front panel of the EIM PSU, the amber lamp below CB1 goes off.
3 
On the interface cabinet, switch CB13 to OFF to disconnect the electrical supply to the UPS.

5.38.3
Examining the operation of the emergency down drive
1 
Start the digital accelerator to supply the 24VACHOST signal to the EIM cabinet.
2 
Set the digital accelerator to the Preparatory machine state.
3 
Move the treatment table to its highest position.
4 
Operate the EMERGENCY STOP button in the treatment room wall to simulate a failure to
the electrical power supply.
This removes the electrical power supply and the 24VACHOST signal from the EIM cabinet.
5 
Make sure that the operation of the ENABLE bar on each user interface module causes the
treatment table to move down.
6 
After six minutes:
a
Make sure that the LEDs in the buttons of each user interface module stay on.
This shows that the UPS has not shut down and the UPS battery is in a good condition.
b
Make sure that the ENABLE bar of each user interface module causes the treatment
table to move down.
7 
Reset the EMERGENCY STOP button in the treatment room.
This switches on the electrical power supply and supplies the 24VACHOST signal to the EIM
cabient.
8 
Set the digital accelerator to the Preparatory machine state.
9 
At the TCS, do a system shutdown.
This removes the electrical power supply to the EIM cabinet, but continues to supply the
24VACHOST signal.
10 Make sure that the LEDs in the buttons of each user interface module go off.
–
If the EDD Timer Module is installed (machines before Serial No. 152531), the UPS shuts
down after approximately 5 minutes (±1 minute). If necessary, you can adjust this time
at the EDD timer module.
–
If the EDD Timer Module is not installed (machines from Serial No. 152531), the UPS
shuts down after approximately 1 minute (±30 seconds).

5.41.12

5.41.12.1
Description of fine-tuning the movement servos of the treatment table
This is a description of the the sequence to fine-tune the movement servos of the treatment
table. These procedures are applicable for Integrity™ TCS, with triple potentiometers.
The procedures to fine-tune the movement servos of the treatment table are applicable for all
the movement systems, which are the:
•
Longitudinal
•
Lateral
•
Height
•
Iso-rotation.
Fine-tune the movement servos of all the movement systems from the control room. Use the
CCTV cameras in the treatment room to see the effect of the adjustments on the treatment
table. Remove all the unwanted equipment near the treatment table before you do the
procedures.
The procedures tune the parameters of each movement servo in the sequence that follows:
•
The slow down point and position gain parameters
•
The threshold parameter
•
The acceleration limit parameter
•
The ASU increment and deadband parameters.

treatment table goes farther than the set position in one

For small movements, it is possible that the position correction
does not give sufficient drive to stop the friction on the motorl.
If the software senses no movement, it applies a Table ASU
correction. Part 142 increases the Table ASU correction at each
cycle (120 ms intervals) of the control system software. These
increases continue until movement occurs. When movement
occurs, the software sets the Table ASU correction to 0 again.
The Table ASU correction applies a series of small movements
(nudges) that move the treatment table to the set position. The
size of the Table ASU correction decreases as the treatment
table moves nearer to that position. Therefore, the amplitude of
the Table ASU correction that is necessary to move the
treatment table will increase. The Table ASU correction will
make a sawtooth plot in which the amplitude increases. Part
142 has a range of 0 to 5.
140
Deadband
The software does not apply Table ASU correction unless the
treatment table position error is more than the value of Part
140. This stops small oscillations about the set position, but
decreases the accuracy of the treatment table position. If you
make a plot of the Table ASU correction against time, and at the
same time press the Table ASU buttons for approximately 10 to
15 seconds:
•
The sawtooth plot will have one to five peaks
•
The amplitude of each peak increases.
Part 140 has a range of 0 to 10, where each unit is 0.2 mm (or
0.2°).

Fine-tuning the ASU increment
This is the procedure to examine the service graph and fine-tune the ASU increment on a
movement servo on the treatment table. This is the applicable procedure for Integrity™ TCS with
triple potentiometers.
1 
Examine the service graph. (This is for Part 137 only).
Note:
Part 142 (which is usually set to 1) has an effect on the slope of the saw-tooth plot. If the value of
Part 142 increases, the slope of the sawtooth line increases, and the time between nudges
decreases. A value of 0 disables the nudge function.
2 
Set Part 142 to the lowest value (usually 2). This will let the treatment table move to the
necessary position in 6 to 8 seconds.
3 
If the treatment table is not in the necessary position in 6 to 8 seconds, you must make an
adjustment:
a
To decrease the time for the treatment table to move to the necessary position,
increase the value of Part 142. It has a maximum value of 5.
b
If the value of Part 142 is too high, it is possible that the treatment table will oscillate or
go through the set position (the correction intermittently changes from positive to
negative). If this occurs, decrease the value of Part 142 by 1 or 2 from its current
setting.
4 
Continue to adjust the ASU increment and deadband until the ASU is stable, with no
oscillation and in a time between 6 and 8 seconds.

6.3.3
Elements of a signal name
Signal names have three elements:
•
The first three letters of the signal name identify the item being driven by the signal.
•
The next letter identifies the movement axis.
•
The next three letters identify the source of the signal.
A line (bar) immediately above the name of a digital signal is an indication that the signal is
active-low (logic 0). For example:
MBKXYLTU
The names of digital signals that do not have a line (bar) immediately above the name are activehigh (logic 1).
